top.title: Nathan Lyon, Marnus Labuschagne dropped! Pat Cummins continues as captain as Australia announce squad for New Zealand series
top.description: Jack Clayton and Corey Rocchiccioli have received their first-ever Test call-ups after being included in Australia's 13-member squad for the upcoming four-match series against New Zealand. The selection, however, comes with a notable omission, with veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon left out of the Pat Cummins-led group. Clayton, a Queensland batter, has earned his place following an impressive run of performances in the Sheffield Shield. Western Australia off-spinner Rocchiccioli has also been rewarded for his consistent returns in domestic cricket and for Australia A. Australia squad: Pat Cummins (c), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Jack Clayton, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Michael Neser, Matthew Renshaw, Corey Rocchiccioli, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc. One additional player will be named following the sixth round of the Sheffield Shield. The 27-year-old Clayton, a left-handed batter, has accumulated 2,732 runs in first-class cricket at an average of 40.17. His record includes seven centuries and 16 half-centuries. He has been particularly prolific in the ongoing Sheffield Shield campaign, scoring 449 runs from nine innings at an average of 74.83, including a century and four fifties. Rocchiccioli, meanwhile, has claimed 18 wickets in the Sheffield Shield this season at an average of 33.88. The 29-year-old has an overall tally of 205 wickets from 59 first-class appearances, with six five-wicket hauls to his name. There are several other changes to Australia's squad that featured in the third Test against South Africa. Marnus Labuschagne, Beau Webster, Cooper Connolly and Matthew Kuhnemann have all been left out, while Nic Maddinson and Sam Harper, who were released ahead of that Test, have not been recalled. Labuschagne endured a disappointing outing in South Africa, finishing the series with 131 runs from six innings at an average of 21.83. His highest score was 39. Lyon, who played two Tests, picked up six wickets at 43.66, with his best figures being 2 for 58. Webster managed 64 runs across four innings in the first two Tests against South Africa, while Connolly, who was part of the playing XI for the series-deciding Cape Town Test, scored 29 runs in two innings and picked up one wicket. However, Lyon's absence stands out as the most significant selection call. Australia's chair of selectors George Bailey admitted that leaving out the experienced off-spinner was a tough decision but stressed that he remained an important part of the team's plans. "Nathan has not quite had the impact we would like with the ball in recent matches," George Bailey, Australia's chair of selectors said. "We also know he has an extraordinary record and his experience, knowledge and skill can still be valuable to the program we have moving forward." The four-Test series against New Zealand begins on December 9, with Perth hosting the opening encounter. The teams will then travel to Adelaide, Melbourne and Sydney for the remaining three matches. top.description: Texas wide receiver Cam Coleman (8) taunts Texas A&M corner Dezz Ricks (2) after a touchdown during the Lone Star Showdown at Kyle Field on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026 in College Station, Texas. On Friday, No. 3 Texas had its defense lead the way to a 16-6 win over Texas A&M at Kyle Field. With its fourth straight win in this in-state rivaly, Texas (10-2, 7-2) advances to play Georgia in next weekend's SEC Championship Game at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The Longhorns got some offense in Friday's victory as Cam Coleman hauled in a touchdown and Gianni Spetic kicked three field goals. But any postgame game balls belonged to a defense that held Texas A&M to 234 yards of offense while recording two sacks and forcing one turnover and two turnover on downs. top.title: 3 quick takeaways from Badgers blowout win over Minnesota: Pure dominance in the trenches
top.description: MADISON, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 27: Colton Joseph #1 of the Wisconsin Badgers scores on a 7 yard touchdown run in the second quarter against the Minnesota Golden Gophers at Camp Randall Stadium on November 27, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers were in dire need of a rivalry win, and they got that on Friday night, beating the Minnesota Gophers 28-5 to reclaim the Axe for the first time in three years. Wisconsin was completely dominant on both sides, putting together another complete win after their 42-10 beatdown of the Purdue Boilermakers last weekend. As a result, they got their first eight-win season under Luke Fickell, putting a bow on an up-and-down season with a much-needed win. Here are three quick takeaways from the Badgers 28-5 win over Minnesota on Friday. Dominance in the trenches As I said pregame, I thought the Badgers would win because they were able to win the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball. That’s exactly what happened as Wisconsin out-gained Minnesota 482-115. The Badgers averaged 5.2 yards per carry, with Colton Joseph eclipsing 100 rushing yards for the second straight game. Defensively, the Badgers held star running back Darius Taylor to just 14 rushing yards, as the Gophers averaged just 0.9 yards per carry. Wisconsin also consistently got pressure on the quarterback, disrupting the Gophers passing attack, leading to them scoring just three offensive points. It felt like this game would come down to trench play. And Wisconsin was the clear winner there. Third downs Wisconsin did a great job offensively getting itself in third-and-manageable scenarios, and they ended up converting 9 of 16 third downs. The Badgers averaged just a 5.8-yard-to-go distance, which allowed them to keep run options open. On the flip side, the Badgers consistently kept Minnesota in third-and-long, with the Gophers averaging 9.7 yards to go. They only converted 2 of 11 third downs, going three-and-out six times. Wisconsin also had some huge third-down plays. Their first touchdown came on a 3rd & 13, with Colton Joseph connecting with Tyrell Henry on a corner route for a 27-yard score. The Badgers also had a big catch-and-run from Colton Joseph on their long drive in the second quarter on 3rd & 5, going for 34 yards. Wisconsin would eventually score a touchdown on the drive. Then, in the fourth quarter, Eugene Hilton took an end around for 42 yards on 3rd & 4, getting the Badgers in the red zone. They would end up not scoring due to an interception, but overall, the Badgers did a great job on third downs. Significance of the Axe The Badgers badly needed to get the Axe back. They had lost this matchup the last two times and four times in the last five games. Not to mention, there were a ton of reports gauging Luke Fickell’s job security. top.description: Anything can be the star of a Far Side comic . top.description: (Photo by Pim Waslander/Soccrates/Getty Images) | Getty Images Falk says there was no gentleman’s agreement (Sport Bild’s Christian Falk) Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala have been in a spat all week, but the battle seems to have subsided as both parties have agreed to take this fight off the streets. One of the more intriguing aspects of the story was whether there was a “gentlemen’s agreement” in place for Musiala to take a pay cut if his health did not improve. That always seems like a longshot, but there were some other interesting tidbits in the report: ❌It is NOT TRUE: Bayern had a gentlemen’s agreement (from the summer) with Jamal Musiala’s side that they could alter the contract. It’s true that there was a meeting at Uli Hoeneß’s residen ce in Tegernsee. I’ve been there a few times myself – quite often, I can say! I know a meeting took place, bu t there was absolutely no agreement with regard to what would or wouldn’t happen with the contract. They made a strategy, at this point, in terms of what would happen if this topic became public and how they could handle the situation with the medication. It was all about how Bayern could help Musiala in these special circumstances. Of course, ev eryone is more than aware of the fact that when two people are talking, sometimes not everyone hears the same thing. So, perhaps there was a little wish from the Bayern side that there could be something implemented so that there could be a later discussion about the financial side of things. But no, this just wasn’t a topic . There were some rumblings earlier in the week about the “gentlemen’s agreement” being nonsense, but that was only part of what interested me. Tennessee football is preparing for another quarterback change ahead of its regular-season finale against Vanderbilt . George MacIntyre is reportedly expected to get the starting nod for the Volunteers in Saturday’s matchup. There were questions surrounding Tennessee’s quarterback situation moving forward, particularly after the Volunteers used both MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon during their 27-13 victory over LSU . However, according to On3 insiders Chris Low and Pete Nakos, the coaching staff has decided to give MacIntyre the starting opportunity against Vanderbilt. “George MacIntyre is set to start at quarterback for Tennessee against Vanderbilt, On3’s Chris Low and Pete Nakos reported. Faizon Brandon is also expected to see play during the Week 13 matchup on Saturday,” Nick Schultz of On3 wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) MacIntyre was still working his way back from an injury when Brandon received the opportunity to start against LSU. However, Tennessee eventually brought both quarterbacks into the game and ultimately won it. The win improved Tennessee’s overall record to 9-2 and its SEC record to 6-2. MacIntyre initially suffered the injury during the Volunteers’ Week 11 victory over Texas A&M. His absence forced the coaching staff to turn to Brandon for the starting responsibilities against LSU. Through nine appearances this season, MacIntyre has recorded 1,041 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. The LSU matchup saw MacIntyre enter the game after Brandon encountered difficulties in the passing game. Meanwhile, Brandon has also put together an encouraging season, recording 732 passing yards, nine touchdowns and two interceptions. He has also demonstrated his dual-threat ability, adding 307 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns. Though MacIntyre is expected to start against Vanderbilt, Brandon’s anticipated involvement suggests that head coach Josh Heupel could continue utilizing both quarterbacks to take advantage of their different skill sets. The Volunteers enter their regular-season finale with significant postseason aspirations. top.description: Jayson Tatum Breaks Silence on Struggles as Celtics' Problems Continue Against Hawks originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Celtics came into the season with championship expectations, but right now they're just trying to stop the brutal losses after brutal losses. After an 87-86 loss to the Hawks, Boston has dropped five of its last six games, and the problems are hard to ignore. Jayson Tatum didn’t play well, and he knows it. Pritchard had a night to forget again, going 3-12. Ultimately, the bigger question is what happens on the nights Tatum isn't at his best. The Celtics used to find ways to win those games, and right now Boston isn't. I’m glad that he’s taking accountability, as he’s at fault, but there are other problems, too. top.title: Kentucky Basketball loses in epically bad fashion to Wichita State in OT: 3 things to know and postgame mourning
top.description: The first-half shooting was as cold inside Rupp Arena on Friday night as the weather outside. Kentucky Basketball opened 4-of-13 from the field in the first eight minutes, and the only thing keeping the Wildcats afloat was Wichita State shooting 4-of-17. Even with both teams ice cold, the Shockers were already bullying Kentucky on the offensive glass, grabbing seven offensive rebounds in the opening eight minutes on their way to [15+] for the night. Kentucky eventually found a spark, ripping off a 12-0 run capped by a Mason Williams three-pointer to build a 31-25 halftime lead. It was about as good as the Cats have looked against a non-buy opponent all season. As always, though, the question with this team is whether it can sustain that level of play. Per the norm this year, Kentucky could not. Wichita State’s Jordan Frison outscored the Wildcats by himself over the first eight minutes of the second half, pouring in 13 points to Kentucky’s 11 and pushing the Shockers ahead 47-42. From there, it turned into a rock fight. Michael Gray Jr. scored 10 of Wichita State’s final 14 points in regulation to knot the game at 65 with 47 seconds left. After a wild Mason Williams miss, Kentucky barely escaped with a chance to win in overtime. A deflected inbounds pass from Braydon Hawthorne and a Milan Momcilovic defensive play forced Will Berg into a tough fadeaway jumper that clanged off the back rim. In overtime, the teams traded blows. Milan Momcilovic stepped out of bounds with just over 30 seconds left while Kentucky trailed by two. Instead of fouling, Kentucky played it out and somehow got the ball back with five seconds remaining. But a coaching blunder left Alex Wilkins throwing the ball to Mason Williams out of bounds. That is only legal after a made basket. Wichita State threw the ball long on the ensuing inbound, and Franck Kepnang intercepted it with a chance to go to the basket. Instead, he passed it back to Momcilovic, whose open three-pointer fell off the rim. Wichita State wins it, 73-71. The epitome of brutality. Here are three things to know from another disastrous performance for Mark Pope and his Wildcats. Kentucky’s effort on the glass was atrocious I knew it was going to be tough, you knew it was going to be tough, and the coaching staff knew it was going to be tough without Malachi Moreno. Still, the players flat-out failed to block out. Wichita State finished with 23 offensive rebounds, which is just absurd at home. Seven-foot-two center Will Berg finished with 20 rebounds, and Dillon Battie had 17. Each of those two players had more rebounds than Kentucky’s entire starting frontcourt of Ousmane N’Diaye, Milan Momcilovic, and Franck Kepnang combined, which finished with just 13. Overall, Wichita State destroyed Kentucky on the glass, 55-36. Missing Moreno hurts, no doubt, but boxing out is about effort, and Kentucky did not bring enough of it. top.description: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this space, we look at the Green Bay Packers’ snap-to-hold operation on field goals and extra points, after years of discussion about the team’s long snapping situation. Much like last week , we only have three this week: two field goals and an extra point. We look at this in two main ways: accuracy and timing. We start by looking at the snap accuracy to the holder. Once again, aided by my 8-year-old son (who asks me every week if he can help me with this). We’ll list the timing for each kick. Based on conversations I’ve had, these are the ranges we’re looking for: Snap-to-holder: 0.28-0.34 Snap-to-kick: 1.2-1.28 Speaking of which, a pretty notable holder said 1.2 to 1.3 seconds is the snap-to-kick range teams are hoping for. Good morning beautiful people.. I’d love to dive more into the FG operation and how things have changed since Ray Finkle’s days Back then, Tightends/Defensive Ends/Etc. did the long snapping on the side.. now it’s a full time gig due to the precision and timing of everything.… pic.twitter.com/bCTEvpW6rs — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 27, 2026 Kick 1: 53-yard field goal (Make) Snap is a little high, up at the facemask of Whelan, but Whelan is able to make an effortless catch and get the ball down for a nice hold. The spin on the snap is good, allowing Whelan to catch the ball by the laces and place the ball with no rotation. Karl Brooks [94] is going against Myles Garrett [95] on the left side. Snap process is a bit slower than you’d like to see, so Garrett gets close, but doesn’t get as close as he did on the first kick. top.title: How Vero Beach football clinched trip back to Florida state semifinals
top.description: VERO BEACH – To combat Edgewater’s ball-control offense, the Vero Beach High football team had to play a little keep away of its own. Unleashing their lightning and thunder backfield, the Fighting Indians were more than productive. Jayden Lockhart scored three touchdowns and combined with running mate Marc Johns for 276 yards on the ground in Vero Beach’s impressive 38-23 victory over the Eagles in the Class 6A-Region 2 final Friday evening, Nov. 27 at Billy Livings Field at the Citrus Bowl. Winners of 10 straight, Vero Beach (12-1) moves into the state semifinals for the second straight year against an undetermined opponent Friday but likely at home. The MaxPreps computer rankings will spit out updated rankings after all the regionals have been completed. Entering the playoffs, Vero Beach ranked second among the teams remaining in Class 6A, behind only Miami Palmetto, which lost to Western, 35-21. Get discount to stream games on NFHS Network Passing attack clicks early Against an Edgewater team that runs the ball 78% of the time, Vero Beach held the Eagles on a three-and-out on their first possession and scored the first three times it had the ball. Another hot start by quarterback Makai White got Vero Beach on the board early. White hit four different receivers in the 49-yard drive, including Marcus Melbourne for a 15-yard touchdown 5 ½ minutes into the game. “It’s good we were able to get out early and stay pretty balanced,” Vero Beach coach Lenny Jankowski said. “We had some success throwing the ball in that first drive. I thought we were able to set the run up. Our O-line did a great job. Coaches did a great job on preparation. And our backs ran really hard.” Snyder Arbelaez booted a 36-yard field goal on Vero Beach’s second possession. After Edgewater (8-5) got on the board with a field goal, Vero Beach unleashed its running attack. nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure For Mrs Usman, the day started like any other school day. Her husband went to pick up their two children from Oakland Kids Nursery and Primary School, Oda Road, Akure, not knowing that their little daughter would come home with a story that would change their family forever. How father heard Her father overheard the conversation. Worried, he called the little girl and asked her to explain. She mentioned the name of her classmate and said he touched her private part. Her father immediately called her mother. At first, Mrs. Usman thought it might be a child’s misunderstanding. But when she got home after 7pm, she checked her daughter’s pants and saw blood stains. And when the child urinated, she cried out in pain. Asked again who touched her, she repeated the same name. Asked why she did not tell her teachers, the little girl said she was afraid she would be beaten. Nightmare, search for healthcare That night, the family rushed to a nearby pharmacy. After examination, doctors confirmed the child had been defiled. With the medical report in hand, she went straight to the school to report. ‘CCTV not working’ According to her, the proprietor expressed shock. Rodriguez’s goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida. The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup. For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS’s top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested. Miami, facing a must-win game after dropping the opener at home to seventh-seeded Columbus, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio. German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar. The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter’s defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair. Miami’s early exit extends the champion’s curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012. nigeria.title: Uduere Killings in Delta: Six trucks of policemen, yet bullets still found targets
nigeria.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi The sound of gunfire shattered the campaign atmosphere at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, November 23. People who had gathered for a political rally suddenly scrambled for safety. Women ran, campaigners scattered and, in the ensuing chaos, bullets found human targets. By the time the shooting stopped, families had lost loved ones, several people critically wounded and communities plunged into mourning. Among the disturbing details was that six truckloads of policemen had reportedly been deployed to provide security. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, put their number at close to 50. Yet, according to accounts from both political camps, the violence escalated despite the robust security presence. The tragedy has since generated competing accusations between the All Progressives Congress, APC, and the National Democratic Congress, NDC. Beneath the political blame game are grieving families, wounded survivors and ordinary citizens asking why a political gathering should become a death trap. A Trail Of Troubled Political Gatherings Uduere was not an isolated incident in the build-up to Delta 2027 elections. September 18, a one-million-man march organised by the NDC in the Warri-Effurun axis was disrupted by violence, leaving persons wounded. An AK-47 allegedly recovered from a suspect identified as Collins became a subject of controversy between the party and police. The NDC alleged the suspect was released the following day, a claim that formed part of its subsequent complaints about police handling of the incident. October 3, the party held a 10,000-man march against hunger in Ughelli. The following day, the Ughelli North Local Government Council, chaired by Chief Jaro Egbo, issued a notice, sealed the business premises and impounded truck belonging to Tobore Alex Agbah, who led the march. Agbah would later become one of the victims of the Uduere violence. November 7, another NDC one-million-man march in Asaba ended in violence, with one fatality recorded. The recurrence of disturbances has fuelled allegations that NDC gatherings are being targeted by political opponents allegedly linked to the ruling APC. Delta State Commissioner for Information, Charles Aniagwu, however, rejected the suggestion of a pattern. “It’s not a pattern, because when you talk about a pattern, it means that it’s continuously and then you are linking it to be able to join one to the other,” he said. nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), about seven weeks before the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. He said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV, v,lidation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. He told the gathering that the rehearsal was as much a test of coordination with security agencies as of technology. “Strategy without rehearsal is merely aspiration,” he said. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. nigeria.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled for survival as the overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Some of the political parties that will be on the ballot have already hit the streets campaigning. Many of the candidates are seeking to renew the mandate that was given to them in 2023. Others who didn’t make it in the last election are back again hoping to succeed this time around. The candidates are making fresh promises. The electorate, on their part, have been speaking on what will inform their choice of who to vote for during the elections and their responses reveal an electorate pulled in sharply different directions. We did not embark on data collation but randomly spoke with some Nigerians in the southwest, southeast, south south and the northern region of the country. Backers of President Bola Tinubu defend him on his capacity to push restructuring and take bold decisions, arguing that but for him the economy would have collapsed completely, even as some concede that his reforms have yet to ease hardship. But they have hope and argue that Nigeria would be better under Tinubu in the years to come. A few voices break from the Obi-Tinubu argument entirely, backing Atiku, the ADC, or local candidates on performance. Another powerful theme in their responses is the widespread distrust of the electoral system itself. Many voters express lack of faith in the process and expect politicians to rig and litigate rather than accept the people’s verdict, even as the spate of ongoing violence is already scaring them. Professionals frame their choices more cautiously arguing that they will be guided by candidates’ positions on sustainable development, Niger Delta equity and resource justice rather than ethnicity or party. However, Emegha has chosen to represent the Netherlands internationally. He made his senior debut against Poland in November 2025, explaining that the Netherlands is his country and that he is proud to be Dutch. Although Nigeria missed out on having him represent the Super Eagles, his progress at Chelsea gives Nigerian fans another reason to follow his career closely. nigeria.title: Chelsea beaten at Nottingham Forest as poor run continues
nigeria.description: Nottingham Forest claimed a memorable 3-2 victory over Chelsea at the City Ground on Friday night, November 27, piling further pressure on Blues manager Xabi Alonso after another disappointing performance from his side. Forest made a flying start to the encounter, taking the lead just five minutes into the game through Igor Jesus, who produced a superb volley from Daniel Muñoz’s cross to put the hosts ahead. Chelsea struggled to find their rhythm in the opening half, with Forest looking more dangerous and organised in attack. Despite enjoying more possession, the visitors failed to turn their dominance on the ball into meaningful goalscoring opportunities. The hosts doubled their advantage shortly after the restart when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the penalty spot in the 51st minute. The penalty was awarded after Wesley Fofana brought down Liam Delap inside the Chelsea box. nigeria.title: A Weekend For Proof
nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

nigeria.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
nigeria.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. The reported immigration charges do not amount to convictions for romance fraud. The post Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand appeared first on Vanguard News .

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. entertainment.title: Remembering Pete Edochie: 5 Films That Made Him a Nollywood Legend
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Did you grow up watching Pete Edochie in Nollywood films? Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . Pete Edochie and Genevieve Nnaji behind the scenes on the set of the 2018 film Lionheart, where they played father and daughter Chief Ernest Obiagu and Adaeze Obiagu. Survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, including actors Linc and Yul Edochie , he leaves behind a remarkable body of work. As we remember his life and contribution to Nigerian cinema, here are five films that capture some of the performances that made Pete Edochie a household name. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). The Longhorns got some offense in Friday's victory as Cam Coleman hauled in a touchdown and Gianni Spetic kicked three field goals. But any postgame game balls belonged to a defense that held Texas A&M to 234 yards of offense while recording two sacks and forcing one turnover and two turnover on downs. technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. technology.title: Lloyds and Bank of Scotland apps fall over on payday
technology.description: Lloyds Bank and Bank of Scotland customers reported problems accessing online banking and transferring money on Friday morning. Reports on Downdetector began rising around 1000 UTC. Lloyds also acknowledged problems on its service status page . A reader who supplied the screenshot below noted the particularly awkward timing: the last Friday of the month is payday for many workers. It's also retail silly season: while Brits don't celebrate Thanksgiving, many UK outlets nonetheless participate in Black Friday sales, meaning storefronts are losing out. Others are concerned with more practical purchases. One customer tweeted that she had "no food at home and cannot shop because I cannot transfer funds from my secondary Lloyds account to my main one. At this point I'm just going to withdraw every penny the moment I'm paid, so much for Internet banking. Never had this years ago." Bank of Scotland, another Lloyds Banking Group brand, reported similar problems on its service status page : " We're aware some customers are having issues with our app and online banking at the moment. We're sorry about this and are working hard to fix it." Earlier this year, a botched overnight software update at Lloyds Banking Group potentially exposed other customers' transaction information to almost 448,000 app users. In a letter to Parliament's Treasury Committee, consumer relationships CEO Jasjyot Singh blamed a defect in the API handling transaction data. The incident affected Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland, and prompted goodwill payments to thousands of customers. Lloyds Banking Group said late last year that it had more than 21 million mobile app users and over 23 million digitally active customers. A spokesperson for Lloyds Banking Group told The Register : "We're aware some customers are having difficulty accessing the app this morning. We’re sorry for the inconvenience and are working to get things back to normal as quickly as possible." ®

technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

science.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

science.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
science.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
science.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? science.title: Astronomers watch a red giant star greedily devour a stellar 'Bao bun' before erupting: 'We couldn't quite believe our luck'
science.description: null Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. The conclusion of the event AT2025abao was marked by a massive eruption witnessed in Oct. 2025 by two instruments at Caltech's Palomar Observatory: the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Wide-field INfrared Transient ExploreR (WINTER). "The excitement was real," team member Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "We couldn't quite believe our luck. With detailed observations for several years before the merger, for the first time, we now have an unprecedented glimpse of the conditions that lead to such cosmic events." Reconstructing a violent cosmic collision The story of AT2025abao began when astronomers detected a bright flash in the nearby Andromeda galaxy , a region where scientists hadn't expected to see a cosmic explosion. Responding to this unexpected flash, Karambelkar and colleagues set about investigating its cause with a plethora of telescopes. This led to them seeing a slow and continuous brightening over the course of two years, They determined the cause of the flash was a rare stellar merger, the luminous red nova now designated AT2025abao. They linked this to a star called WNTR23bzdiq / WTP19aalzlk that had been observed steadily brightening since 2019 after being stable for the preceding 30 years. Thus, the team determined that at the heart of the event is a red giant, a star that puffs out to hundreds of times its original size after it runs out of hydrogen in its core. The team theorizes that Big Bao, with a mass seven times greater than the sun, expanded so rapidly and violently that it swallowed its smaller companion star. The unfortunate star, Little Bao, then spiraled into Big Bao's core in fewer than 10 orbits. "A couple of years back, we discovered a star that was gradually brightening. We took a closer look to discover a red giant, or a star that has started to expand toward the end of its life, just like our sun will one day," Karambelkar said. "Steady brightening was unusual, but even if something was stirring, no one expected to see an explosion in their lifetime, as these stars remain relatively stable for thousands of years." science.description: A detail from Joseph Wright’s 1771 painting The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus, showing Henning Brand in 1669 Science History Images/Alamy Imagine you could boil the development of science down to a single ingredient. A magical, mystical compound that transformed human history. Of course, science doesn’t work that way; even if breakthroughs shift the paradigm of our understanding, discovery doesn’t progress like a tech tree in a computer game, but as an interweaving tapestry of complementary and competing ideas and experimentation. Theories can bubble under the surface for centuries, overlooked because of politics or failure to realise their implications, while innovations can emerge from taking an idea in one industry and transplanting it to another. But, for a moment, try and picture what just one such ingredient could be. What would you pick? For centuries, in medieval Europe, alchemists quested for the “Philosopher’s Stone” that would finally help them achieve their dreams of transmutation. It was a search doomed to failure from the very beginning. And yet, a far better idea was under their noses – or, rather, their underpants – the entire time. My pick? Urine has a strong case for being the most transformative substance in human history. It required the first chemical reaction we mastered – fire – to keep us warm, cook our food and smelt ores. But leatherwork played an equally key role. Urine is a source of urea, which bacteria can break down into ammonia, granting early humans easy access to a base that could soften organic matter and tan hides. Across the world, leatherwork became the cornerstone of survival for every civilisation, from the Americas to Europe, Africa and Asia: even cultures that didn’t develop a bronze age, such as the Aztec, or skipped it entirely, as seen in Sub-Saharan Africa, relied on leatherwork for clothes, structures, industry and commerce. When the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image on November 8, 2026, clouds encroached on the snowy mountain on Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula . But they hovered beneath the volcano’s 3,283-meter (10,771-foot) peak, leaving a clear opening over its caldera and northern upper slopes. Lava domes on Shivelyuch go through cycles of growth and collapse, with collapses sometimes setting off fast-moving avalanches of hot ash and rock called pyroclastic flows . In November 2026, effusive eruptions of lava and explosive activity at Shivelyuch had been ongoing for months , according to reports from the Kamchatka Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT). And despite frequent cloudiness, satellites regularly detect thermal anomalies from the volcano. On the day of this image, KVERT reported that a plume of resuspended ash drifted 120 kilometers (75 miles) to the east. That kind of activity is relatively tame for the mountain. Explosions from Shivelyuch periodically send ash several kilometers up into the atmosphere, where it can travel great distances and pose risks to aircraft .
